_comment: English translation of notation.json. Only text fields are here; ids, categories and status keys come from notation.json. Fields left out keep the Danish value.

types.name: Data types
types.description: Prefixes for elementary data types such as BOOL, INT and REAL.

fb.name: Function blocks
fb.description: Standard blocks such as R_TRIG, F_TRIG, TON and CTU.

scope.name: Scope and parameters
scope.description: Prefixes that show where a variable lives: input, output, global, local.

io.name: I/O and addresses
io.description: Inputs, outputs, markers and hardware addresses.

pou.name: Block names and types
pou.description: Naming of programs, FBs, functions, structures and enums.

rules.name: Best practices
rules.description: General rules for good variable names.

codesys.note: CODESYS' own coding conventions use x for BOOL (b is reserved for BIT).

siemens.note: The Siemens style guide recommends no type prefix. Use a descriptive name, ideally phrased as a question: isRunning, motorOn.

ab.note: No official prefix. Many use b_ or no prefix at all.

codesys.note: Only allowed as an element of a STRUCT or FB.

siemens.note: No separate BIT type. Use Bool or slice access: myWord.%X3.

ab.note: Access a single bit with a dot: MyDint.5
AB has no BYTE. SINT (signed 8 bit) is used instead.
AB has no WORD. INT is used.
AB uses DINT for almost everything, bit patterns included.

codesys.note: USINT (unsigned, 0…255) has the prefix usi.

siemens.note: USInt also exists.

ab.note: Rockwell recommends DINT over SINT/INT, because the controller calculates fastest in 32 bit.

codesys.note: UINT (0…65,535) has the prefix ui.

siemens.note: Analog inputs on S7 are typically Int (0…27,648 = 0…100 %).

ab.note: Prefer DINT, unless the data has to match an external format.

codesys.note: UDINT has the prefix udi.

ab.note: The standard integer type in Logix.

codesys.note: ULINT has the prefix uli.

ab.note: Limited instruction support on older firmware.

valueRange.note: Smallest value near 0: ±1.175494 × 10⁻³⁸. About 7 significant digits.

ab.note: Only on newer controllers and firmware.

valueRange.note: Smallest value near 0: ±2.225074 × 10⁻³⁰⁸. About 15 significant digits.

codesys.note: WSTRING (Unicode) has the prefix ws.

siemens.note: WString for Unicode.

ab.note: Structure with .LEN and .DATA[82].

codesys.note: LTIME has the prefix ltim. Many also use t or tim.

siemens.note: LTime on S7-1500 (ns resolution).

ab.note: No TIME type. The timer preset is a DINT in milliseconds.

valueRange.note: CODESYS: 0 … 4,294,967,295 ms (unsigned). Siemens Time is signed: T#-24d20h31m23s648ms … T#24d20h31m23s647ms.

ab.note: Read with GSV WallClockTime as a DINT array.

codesys.note: DATE has the prefix date.

siemens.note: DTL (structure) is recommended on S7-1200/1500.

ab.note: WallClockTime via GSV.

array.meaning: List of elements of the same type

codesys.note: Prefixes are combined: arTemps = ARRAY OF REAL.

ab.note: Always starts at index 0.

pointer.meaning: Pointer or reference to another variable

siemens.note: Ref_To on S7-1500 only.

ab.note: No pointers. Use InOut or indirect addressing.

rtrig.title: Rising trigger (rising edge)
rtrig.meaning: Q is TRUE for one scan when CLK goes from FALSE to TRUE

codesys.note: Standard IEC block. Instance name e.g. rtStart or fbStartEdge.

siemens.note: In LAD there is the P contact and P_TRIG. R_TRIG needs an instance (multi-instance in an FB).

ab.note: ONS (contact) or OSR (output). Needs a storage bit, e.g. StartButton_ONS.

ftrig.title: Falling trigger (falling edge)
ftrig.meaning: Q is TRUE for one scan when CLK goes from TRUE to FALSE

siemens.note: The N contact in LAD.

ton.title: Timer On-Delay
ton.meaning: Q becomes TRUE when IN has been TRUE for the time PT

codesys.note: Outputs: Q and ET (elapsed time).

siemens.note: Instance as multi-instance or its own DB. Outputs Q and ET.

ab.note: Members: .PRE, .ACC (ms), .EN, .TT, .DN.

tof.title: Timer Off-Delay
tof.meaning: Q stays TRUE for the time PT after IN goes FALSE

tp.title: Timer Pulse
tp.meaning: Gives a pulse of fixed length PT on a rising edge at IN

ab.note: No TP in ladder. Build it with ONS + TON, or use TONR/FBD blocks.

ctu.title: Counter Up
ctu.meaning: Counts CV up on every rising edge at CU. Q = CV >= PV

codesys.note: CTD (down) and CTUD (up/down) also exist.

ab.note: Members: .PRE, .ACC, .CU, .DN, .OV, .UN.

sr.meaning: Remembers a state. SR: set is dominant. RS: reset is dominant

ab.note: Latch and unlatch coils in ladder.

fb-instance.title: Instance of your own function block
fb-instance.meaning: Variable that is an instance of an FB

siemens.note: The instance DB is automatically named after the FB + _DB.

ab.note: E.g. Motor1 : AOI_Motor.

codesys.note: E.g. inxStart or i_xStart. Pick one style and stick to it.

siemens.note: Siemens shows the section itself. The style guide uses camelCase without a prefix.

codesys.note: q_ follows the IEC letter Q for output.

inout.title: In/Out parameter (VAR_IN_OUT)
inout.meaning: Variable passed in by reference that can be changed

ab.note: The only way to pass arrays and structures by reference.

codesys.note: With {attribute 'qualified_only'} you write GVL.name, so a prefix is not needed.

siemens.note: Global data is written as "DB_name".variable.

ab.note: Use program-scoped tags where possible.

codesys.note: Most people only use a type prefix for local variables.

siemens.note: Temp variables are not kept between scans. Some use tmp_ for Temp.

const.title: Constant
const.meaning: Value that cannot be changed at runtime

codesys.note: Many write constants in UPPER_CASE: MAX_SPEED.

siemens.note: The style guide uses UPPER_CASE for constants.

retain.meaning: Kept through power loss or restart

codesys.note: Avoid r_ if you also use r for REAL. Prefer ret_.

ab.note: Logix keeps tag values by default.

di.title: Digital input
di.meaning: Physical digital signal into the PLC (e.g. push button, sensor)

codesys.note: Map I/O to variables in the I/O mapping.

siemens.note: German notation uses E (Eingang) instead of I.

ab.note: Create alias tags with meaningful names.

do.title: Digital output
do.meaning: Physical digital signal out of the PLC (e.g. relay, valve)

siemens.note: German notation: A (Ausgang).
Raw value 0…27648. Scale with NORM_X and SCALE_X.

ab.note: Modules can scale directly to engineering units.

ao.title: Analog output
ao.meaning: Analog signal out (e.g. frequency converter speed reference)

marker.title: Marker / internal memory
marker.meaning: Internal bit or word in the PLC's memory

codesys.note: Prefer symbolic variables.

siemens.note: The style guide advises against markers. Use DBs instead.

ab.note: Logix is fully tag based.

prg.meaning: Program POU called from a task

codesys.note: MAIN is often just called MAIN.

siemens.note: OB1 = Main, OB100 = startup, OB30-38 = cyclic.

ab.note: MainRoutine is the default.

siemens.note: Style guide: PascalCase without a prefix, e.g. Conveyor. The FB_ prefix is still very common though.

fc.title: Function
fc.meaning: Block without memory that returns a value

struct.title: Structure (user-defined type)
struct.meaning: Collection of variables in one type

siemens.note: The style guide uses the prefix typ, e.g. typMotor.

codesys.note: Use {attribute 'qualified_only'} so you write E_State.Idle.

siemens.note: TIA has no ENUM. Use constants of type Int.

ab.note: No ENUM. Use DINT constants.

siemens.note: Not supported in classic TIA (but available in SIMATIC AX).

rule-descriptive.title: Descriptive names
rule-descriptive.meaning: The name should say what the variable is, not how it happens to be used right now

codesys.note: Good: xConveyorRunning. Bad: x1, temp, flag3.

siemens.note: Style guide: use meaningful English names.

ab.note: Use tag descriptions too.

rule-case.title: Upper and lower case
rule-case.meaning: Pick one way of writing and use it everywhere

codesys.note: Lower-case prefix + PascalCase: xMotorOn. Types: FB_Motor.

siemens.note: Variables in camelCase (motorOn), blocks in PascalCase (Motor), constants in UPPER_CASE.

ab.note: Tags are not case sensitive, but use PascalCase or Under_Score for readability.

rule-length.title: Length and allowed characters
rule-length.meaning: Keep names short enough to read in ladder

codesys.note: Only letters, digits and _. Must not start with a digit. No double __.

siemens.note: Up to 128 characters, but short names are easier to read in LAD.

ab.note: Max 40 characters. No double or trailing underscores.

rule-bool-names.title: BOOL as a yes/no question
rule-bool-names.meaning: A boolean name should read as true or false

rule-units.title: Units in the name
rule-units.meaning: Put the unit in the name of physical values

siemens.note: It can also go in the comment, but the name is visible everywhere.

ab.note: Engineering units can be set on analog modules.

rule-consistency.title: Consistency beats perfection
rule-consistency.meaning: Follow the company's or project's standard, even if you personally prefer something else

codesys.note: CODESYS has its own coding conventions in the help and static analysis that can check names.

siemens.note: Siemens Programming Styleguide for S7-1200/S7-1500 (free on Siemens Industry Online Support).

ab.note: Rockwell's Logix 5000 Design Considerations and PlantPAx guides.

rule-consistency.example: Write your naming standard down in the project

rule-rds.title: Link names to the electrical diagram
rule-rds.meaning: Use the reference designation from the electrical drawing (IEC 81346) in the tag name or description

codesys.note: E.g. xB1_LevelHigh, where B1 is the sensor on the drawing.

siemens.note: The comment field is a good place for the full RDS designation.

ab.note: Use an alias tag with the RDS name on the I/O point.

rule-rds.example: xDI_B12_TankFull  (B12 = level sensor on the drawing)
